quarterly_data.quarter: Recursion press release: Recursion Announces $200 Million Oversubscribed Follow-On (10-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: REC-4881 (oral MEK1/2 inhibitor, FAP) topline data from the Phase 1b/2 TUPELO study at 4 mg once daily, including the expanded adult (18+) FAP population (data cutoff September 10, 2026): in the total GI tract, after 12 weeks of treatment 87% of patients had reductions in total polyp burden, with a 47% median reduction, 1 in 3 patients achieved a reduction of 65% or more, and at Week 25 (after a 12-week off-treatment follow-up) 85% were still below baseline. In the upper GI tract, which the company calls the area of greatest unmet need, 92% of patients had reductions after 12 weeks, with a 55% median polyp burden reduction; nearly half achieved a reduction of 65% or more, two patients achieved a >=98% reduction, 50% (6 of 12) improved by at least one Spigelman stage at Week 13, and 92% were still below baseline at Week 25. Safety: no TRAEs above Grade 3; 21 of 26 patients (80.8%) had TRAEs of Grade 2 or lower; Grade 3 TRAEs occurred in 4 patients; four patients discontinued due to AEs, none because of a Grade 3 TRAE.
quarterly_data.figure: total GI: 87% with reductions, 47% median reduction, 85% below baseline at Week 25; upper GI: 92% with reductions, 55% median reduction, 6 of 12 improved one Spigelman stage, 92% below baseline at Week 25; 80.8% TRAEs Grade 2 or lower

quarterly_data.quarter: Recursion press release: Recursion Announces $200 Million Oversubscribed Follow-On (10-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: REC-4881 regulatory path and market: Recursion anticipates initiating a registrational trial in the second half of 2027, pending the outcome of ongoing FDA discussions, and will provide additional details later this year; additional Phase 1b/2 data as of September 10, 2026 will be presented at the CGA-IGC Annual Meeting on November 2. REC-4881 holds FDA Orphan Drug and Fast Track designations. The company puts FAP at more than 50,000 patients in the US and EU5, a potential $15 billion opportunity based on company estimates, with upper GI disease the highest unmet need among approximately 35,000 post-colectomy patients.
quarterly_data.figure: registrational trial initiation targeted 2H 2027; >50,000 patients; potential $15 billion opportunity (company estimate); ~35,000 post-colectomy patients

quarterly_data.quarter: Recursion press release: Recursion Announces $200 Million Oversubscribed Follow-On (10-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: REC-1245 (oral RBM39 molecular glue degrader) early data from the Phase 1 dose-escalation portion of the DAHLIA Phase 1/2 study (data cutoff August 21, 2026): three partial responses per RECIST 1.1 (2 confirmed, 1 unconfirmed) in heavily pretreated patients with endometrial cancer and hepatocellular carcinoma, all at doses of 45 mg once daily or higher, with a disease control rate of 91.7% at those doses (n=12). Recursion selected 45 mg QD for expansion cohorts, including endometrial cancer; at 45 mg QD (n=10) no dose-limiting toxicities or treatment-related serious adverse events were observed, TRAEs were predominantly Grade 1 or 2, and the most frequent were Grade 1 or 2 fatigue and anemia (30% each). Additional Phase 1 monotherapy data are expected in the second half of 2026 and preliminary dose expansion data in endometrial cancer in the second half of 2027; dose escalation continues in other solid tumor indications.
quarterly_data.figure: 3 partial responses (2 confirmed); disease control rate 91.7% (n=12) at >=45 mg; 45 mg QD selected; fatigue and anemia 30% each; expansion data 2H 2027

quarterly_data.quarter: Recursion press release: Recursion Announces $200 Million Oversubscribed Follow-On (10-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Portfolio prioritization: given the REC-4881 and REC-1245 data, Recursion plans to continue to focus resources on its high-impact partnerships and internal pipeline - REC-4881, REC-1245 (RBM39 - endometrial cancer and other solid tumors), REC-4539 (LSD1 - solid tumors and hematology), REC-7735 (PI3K-alpha H1047R - solid tumors) and REC-102 (ENPP1 - hypophosphatasia) - and intends to pursue partnership opportunities to advance REC-617 (CDK7) and REC-3565 (MALT1). CEO Najat Khan: 'Over the past 18 months, we've fundamentally transformed Recursion with a clear ambition: to repeatedly translate AI-driven discoveries into differentiated medicines for patients.'
